nodes.summary: For every integer sequence $(a_i)_{i \ge 0}$ and every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the $n$-th term of the binomial transform of $a$ equals $\sum_{i=0}^{n} \binom{n}{i} a_i$.
nodes.title: Binomial transform as a binomial sum

nodes.summary: The binomial transform of an integer sequence $(a_i)_{i \ge 0}$ is the falling k-binomial transform of $a$ with $k = 1$, the sequence whose $n$-th term is $\sum_{i=0}^{n} \binom{n}{i} 1^{n-i} a_i$.
nodes.title: Binomial transform

nodes.summary: Let $(a_n)_{n \ge 0}$ and $(b_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be real sequences with $b_n = \sum_{k=0}^{n} \binom{n}{k} a_k$ for every $n$, and let $A : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be any function. For every real number $t$, if the series $\sum_{n \ge 0} a_n t^n / n!$ converges absolutely with sum $A(t)$, then the series $\sum_{n \ge 0} b_n t^n / n!$ converges absolutely with sum $e^t A(t)$.
nodes.title: Exponential generating function of the binomial transform

nodes.summary: For every integer sequence $a$ and every integer $k$: if $k \ge 0$, applying the binomial transform $k$ times to $a$ gives the falling $k$-binomial transform of $a$; if $k < 0$, applying the inverse binomial transform (the falling $(-1)$-binomial transform) $-k$ times to $a$ gives the falling $k$-binomial transform of $a$. In both cases the equality is one of integer sequences.
nodes.title: The k-fold binomial transform is the falling k-binomial transform

nodes.title: Generating function of the binomial transform over a field

nodes.summary: The binomial transform sends an integer sequence $(a_i)_{i \ge 0}$ to the sequence $(b_n)_{n \ge 0}$ given by $b_n = \sum_{i=0}^{n} \binom{n}{i} a_i$. For a natural number $r$, the $r$-fold binomial transform of $a$ is obtained by applying the binomial transform $r$ times in succession; the $0$-fold transform of $a$ is $a$ itself.

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
